sources.title: Saudipedia, Basic Law of Governance in Saudi Arabia
sources.note: Direct Ministry of Media encyclopedia article, 1932 name/unification order and 1992 Basic Law. Historical governmental description, not independent certification that promised rights or services are universally delivered.

sources.title: Aramco, Our history
sources.note: Direct company history. 1933 concession, commercial production1938, Tapline1950 and full Saudi government ownership1980. Omit conflicting March3/4 discovery day in company publications.

sources.title: Aramco, The desert pioneer behind our first oil discovery (2025)
sources.note: Direct original corporate history read. Khamis ibn Rimthan navigation and early1940s camel caravans; avoid romanticized supernatural navigation wording or suggesting he single-handedly discovered oil.

sources.title: OPEC, sixty-second anniversary statement (14 September 2022)
sources.note: Direct original organizational statement, Baghdad conference and five named founding states. No claim Saudi Arabia alone sets international oil prices.

sources.title: US Office of the Historian, Oil Embargo, 1973 to 1974
sources.note: Direct institutional historical account. Distinguish Arab exporting participants from all OPEC members and economic crisis from one-cause explanation. Retired historical series; used historical events only.

sources.title: UNESCO, Al-Qatt Al-Asiri, inscription 01261 (2017)
sources.note: Indexed original full description; direct open sometimes human-verification page. Specific to Asir community, not every Saudi household. Therapeutic claim not repeated.

sources.title: UNESCO, Arabic coffee, a symbol of generosity, inscription 02111 (2024)
sources.note: Indexed original full description. Multinational tradition Saudi Arabia shares with Qatar, Oman, UAE and Jordan. 2024 extension; do not mistake listing for invention date.

sources.title: UNESCO, Al-Ahsa Oasis, World Heritage property 1563
sources.note: Direct listing and Outstanding Universal Value; 2018 inscription, 2.5million palms as listing description, spring canal distribution, red rice and markets. Ancient landscape continuing under modern kingdom, not a1932 invention.

sources.title: UNESCO, Historic Jeddah, World Heritage property 1361
sources.note: Direct and indexed original OUV. Late19th-century tower houses, ground-floor commerce and pilgrim rooms, coral masonry and ventilation. Obvious AH/AD error in one historical paragraph omitted.

sources.title: Saudi World Heritage nomination, Historic Jeddah, architectural description
sources.note: Indexed original nomination passage beginning Roshan-s are constructed of louvered panels. Wooden sitting extensions, breeze and clay water pots. Direct full PDF not inspected, no invented page number. Conservatively grouped with the related UNESCO property1361 Jeddah listing for cumulative budgets.

sources.title: King Saud University, History
sources.note: Direct institutional history: 1957 founding, first Arts cohort21 men, first English female cohort4 in1381AH, approximately1961/62. Use year1957 only where exact, no false exact date for1381AH. Avoid promotional universal claims and inconsistent total colleges.

sources.title: King Saud Library, Testimonies and Documents of King Fahd on the Era of King Saud
sources.note: Indexed original royal archive narrative. Separate decree1379AH from opening15 primary schools academic1380 to 1381AH. Preserve Islamic year range rather than misconvert exact Gregorian year.

sources.title: WHO, Saudi Arabia eliminates trachoma as a public health problem (21 February 2022)
sources.note: Direct WHO validation dated26January2022. Elimination as public-health problem, not worldwide eradication or zero possible cases. Care/water/education collaboration in Saudi program; no treatment instructions.

sources.title: UN Secretary-General statement on Saudi Arabia (24 June 2018)
sources.note: Indexed original statement welcomes lifting of driving ban. Direct page anti-bot; dated independent first-party UN reaction.

sources.title: Human Rights Watch, Saudi Arabia: Women’s Rights Advocates Arrested (18 May 2018)
sources.note: Direct contemporary investigation release. Seven defenders detained since15May, named campaigners and source attribution retained. No claim about their present legal or detention status.

sources.title: SAMA, Polymer five-riyal announcement in Arabic (4 October 2020)
sources.note: Full indexed original Arabic announcement verified with query site:sama.gov.sa "البوليمر" "خمسة ريالات" "2020". Direct page now omits body. Exact writing is from first paragraph of dated announcement, not claimed visually inspected on banknote.

sources.title: SAMA, Polymer five-riyal announcement in English (4 October 2020)
sources.note: Full indexed original English parallel, query site:sama.gov.sa "SAMA" "polymer" "Shaybah" "2020". Same work as Arabic announcement; budgets merged. PDF security brochure unavailable and not treated as inspected.

proposedOverrides.name: Saudi Arabia
proposedOverrides.summary: A modern Arabian monarchy shaped by oil, pilgrimage, regional traditions and expanding institutions, proclaimed before this map record begins.

batchIdentityNotes.decision: One exact indexed modern-state record only. No Nejd, Arabia-Nejd or Hejaz phase aliases.
batchIdentityNotes.historicalScope: Kingdom proclamation1932; imported record1938 to null. Public periods follow map onset and1992 Basic Law, not a claim the state began with oil.
batchIdentityNotes.geometry: Six decoded features1938 to 2020. All omit Dammam control point.1938 feature contains Sana’a; later ones do not. All contain Riyadh,Jeddah,Mecca,Medina,Al-Ahsa andAbha. Public overview names serious errors and missingpost2020 polygons.
batchIdentityNotes.writing: Attested2020 Arabic central-bank announcement, not a claimed ancient inscription or visually checked banknote lettering.
